items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: All the bands, just like you hear Shark and Al Wakeman play, well that's the way they was playing.

ctx.x: Back before you went to California, when you were very young, how would the bands play a piece? How you mean? Well, I mean, would they start off loud or soft? Would everybody come in on the beginning?

Yeah, everybody. Everybody. It's like you're shocking them, everybody playing. Ensemble. That's right. That's right. That's right. That would be the beginning, huh? In the beginning. Then all right, if you had your trumpet player, he wanted to take a solo, well you let him take a solo. You take two, you're a trombone player, you're a clarinet player. But most was ensemble, see. Didn't do very much soloing, see. Didn't do very much. All the bands, just like you hear Shark and Al Wakeman play, well that's the way…
But more ensemble. Yeah, oh yeah, yeah.
